title: The stat that matters most for your game's success isn't wishlists
author: maxlopezos
selftext:
I see a lot of people thinking wishlist is the #1 indicator of a game's success, while it helps, i personnally view wishlists as a simple "hype" indicator, and small boost in sales at launch.  
What will truly make your game take off is the fact people actually enjoy playing it for long sessions, and the stat that gives this information away the best is median play time, why ? Because X amount of median playtime = 50% of people played more than this amount and the rest played less.

  
According to how to market a game:

**"Revenue Tier Breakdowns:** Median playtimes vary drastically depending on how well the game performs commercially:

* **Bronze Tier:** \~7 minutes median playtime
* **Silver Tier:** \~18 minutes median playtime
* **Gold Tier:** \~38 minutes median playtime
* **Diamond Tier:** \~65 minutes median playtime"

So if your demo is already above gold, I have some good news for you.  
But careful, if your Lifetime unique user is below 100, the median playtime doesn't mean much yet, you need to gather more data.
